title: Indiana's 8th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Indiana's 8th Congressional District covers southwestern Indiana, including Evansville and Terre Haute. Incumbent Republican Rep. Mark Messmer is seeking a second term after winning the open seat in 2024 following the retirement of longtime Rep. Larry Bucshon (R). Messmer, a former Indiana Senate Majority Leader and small business owner, has focused his campaign on tax cuts, deregulation, and job creation. He faces Democratic nominee Mary Allen, an Evansville City Councilor and Army Reserve veteran, and independent candidate James Burke. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Republican, reflecting the district's conservative lean, though Democrats have expressed increased enthusiasm in 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls found for this race as of June 2026. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solidly Republican.'

candidates.name: Mark Messmer
candidates.summary: Mark Messmer is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Indiana's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. He previously served in the Indiana Senate as Majority Leader and in the Indiana House of Representatives, and is a small business owner who co-founded Messmer Mechanical. Messmer sits on the House Agriculture, Armed Services, and Education & Workforce committees and has positioned himself as a conservative focused on tax relief, reducing federal regulation, and economic development in southwestern Indiana.

candidates.name: Mary Allen
candidates.summary: Mary Allen is an at-large member and vice president of the Evansville City Council and the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 8th Congressional District. She is a small business owner, Army Reserve veteran, and former occupational therapist who co-owns Virginia Street Properties and operates a sustainability-focused store. Allen has centered her campaign on affordability, protecting Medicaid and rural hospitals, raising wages, expanding affordable housing, and reducing the influence of corporate money in politics.

forecast.rationale: No public polls exist for this race as of June 2026, limiting confidence. The forecast relies on structural indicators: incumbent Republican Mark Messmer holds a strongly conservative district (Cook Political Report rates it Solidly Republican), and he benefits from incumbency and a recent 2024 open-seat win following retiring Rep. Larry Bucshon. Democratic nominee Mary Allen is a credible challenger with city council and military experience, and the race description notes increased Democratic enthusiasm in 2026; however, no polling or fundraising data suggests a shift toward competitiveness. Independent James Burke has a minimal public profile and is unlikely to be a factor. Given the district's conservative lean, incumbency, and absence of contrary signals, Republican retention is highly probable.
